correctness.rationale: The frozen sampled-state Itô integral gives iid factors exp(theta*tau)+b*sigma*H_alpha^(1/alpha) S_alpha. Stable subordination S_alpha=V_alpha C for index <=1 and the Cauchy Poisson-log identity yield the exact factor log mean. Stable polynomial tails and bounded density near a cancellation root yield integrability. The interval envelope has an integrable positive logarithm by the p<alpha maximal moment; Borel-Cantelli lifts the sampled strong law to the exact continuous-time limsup. Strictly increasing positive log correction produces the no-stabilization and unique-threshold conclusions. Cauchy threshold algebra and alpha=1/2 independent mixing are included in 253 grouped finite/numerical checks; finite checks do not prove universal claims.

originality.rationale: Closest matched papers were inspected in their relevant mathematical sections. Mao (2016) proves Gaussian stabilization for the same sampled architecture, not alpha<=1 stable non-stabilization. Wang–Gao–Yuan (first public 2025-03-17) treat quasi-sure and mean-square stabilization under G-Lévy noise and sampled feedback, but a complete text comparison was inaccessible. Li et al. (2025) use Lévy perturbation with drift sampling control and squared jump/moment hypotheses. Zhang (2026-11-03) proves a sufficient positive-drift stabilization condition for alpha in (1,2), explicitly requiring p in (0,alpha-1); hence it excludes this alpha<=1 endpoint. The Cauchy mixture, logarithmic Poisson integral, and sampled SLLN are classical and not claimed new. The joint exact heavy-tail obstruction and full all-gain phase classification was not found in literature searches. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An older general theorem on logarithmic potentials of stable random affine products may already imply the exact rate without using this sampled-feedback phrasing.

value.rationale: The tail-index-one stability boundary is a motivated sharp structural phase separation: sampled Gaussian or index>1 Lévy noise can stabilize positive drift under conditions in established literature, whereas every symmetric alpha<=1 sampled gain strictly increases the almost-sure exponent. Exact all-sampling-gap pathwise rate, a unique negative-drift feedback threshold and explicit Cauchy endpoint go beyond a routine scaling or a narrow arbitrary number. The theorem is not claimed for asymmetric noise, drift controls, nonlinear models or finite-moment stability.
